title: Cut each stem part-way, bend it over, and a hedge grows back thicker
alt: A long, freshly laid hedge of cut and bent stems held between upright stakes, running across open fields under a blue sky with a few people working far along it.

posts.facebook:
Cut a stem part-way, bend it over, and it keeps growing. That is how a laid hedge is made.

Done along a whole hedge, it thickens into a barrier that holds in cattle and sheep. The National Hedgelaying Society describes 11 regional styles.

It's a winter job. Beginners' courses run between November and April at agricultural colleges, wildlife trusts (local conservation charities) and rural skills centers. Some conservation volunteer groups lend tools to newcomers. The courses we found are in the UK.

Bring thick trousers (pants, in the US), work gloves, sturdy boots, a hat and a packed lunch.

Would you give it a try?

How to start, and where to go → https://dontdieretired.com/list/learn-hedge-laying/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=things-to-do
